data.body:
`LeaseData` (src/domain/lease.rs:89) carries lease_type, nickname, agent_info,
and timeout_seconds — but no identity for the machine that created the lease.
Lease knots are ordinary synced knots (created via `create_lease` ->
`create_knot_with_options` with `KnotType::Lease`, src/lease.rs:8), so a lease
created on machine A can land in machine B's `knot_hot` through a normal pull.

`count_active_leases` (src/db/catalog.rs:325) filters only on knot_type, state,
and lease_expiry_ts. It cannot tell a locally held lease from a replicated one,
so any active lease that reaches another machine blocks that machine's sync
until the lease's expiry timestamp passes, even though no agent there holds it.

Add an owner identity to leases and make local-lease queries owner-aware. This
is a prerequisite for per-knot sync filtering: "skip knots this machine is
working on" is only expressible once "this machine" is recorded on the lease.

Scope:
- Add an optional `owner` field to `LeaseData` (stable machine id + pid), set
  at creation in `create_lease`.
- Persist and project it through the index event -> knot_hot path so it
  survives sync (see `parse_lease_data` in src/sync/apply_helpers.rs).
- Add `count_local_active_leases` / `list_local_active_leases` that filter to
  the current machine, and switch `require_no_active_leases`
  (src/replication.rs:456) and `sync_or_defer_with_progress` to them.
- Treat a lease with no owner (events written before this change) as local, so
  existing stores keep today's conservative behavior.

Out of scope: removing the sync guard, per-knot filtering. Those are separate
knots.
data.title: Record owning machine on leases so replicated leases cannot block sync
